column3: Month start date — type the 1st of the month you are tracking.
Who is first in line on day 1. Pick from the dropdown once the names below are filled in.

column2: MEMBER NAMES — type the five names here

column3: These names become the column headings on the Timetable sheet and the names shown in the Washer columns, Next Before and Next After.
Rotation order is top to bottom: M1 ? M2 ? M3 ? M4 ? M5 ? back to M1.
Leave a row blank and that person keeps the label M1, M2 and so on.
Renaming later is safe — the whole sheet updates and no history is lost.
Do not reorder the rows; that would swap people's places in the queue.
Pick Yes or No for each meal separately. A day can have lunch only, dinner only, both, or neither.
Pick 1 or 2 — how many people share the lunch vessels that day. Set per day, so heavy days can take two and light days one. Blank or anything other than 2 is treated as 1.
Yellow block = who ate LUNCH. Blue block = who ate DINNER. Type Y for each person who actually ate that meal; leave blank for absent, on leave, or skipped.
Mark each meal separately — someone can eat lunch and miss dinner, or the reverse.
Lunch Washer 1 is the person nearest the front of the queue who ate lunch. Lunch Washer 2 is the next one after them who also ate lunch.
Washer 1 first, then Washer 2, so their order in the queue is preserved for next time.
If only one person ate lunch, Lunch Washer 2 shows —. Nobody is ever picked twice for the same meal, and the missing second slot is not owed to anyone later.
Change the day's Lunch Washers back to 1 and Washer 2 clears, with the queue adjusting straight away.
A single queue covers every washing slot. Lunch is settled first (one or two people), then dinner picks up from the queue as it stands afterwards.

column2: Up to three slots a day
column3: On a both-meals day with two lunch washers, three different people are assigned — two for lunch, one for dinner.
It keeps total workload even. Nobody gets stuck always doing lunch while someone else always does dinner.
The washer is the person nearest the front of the queue who ate that meal. After washing, that person goes to the back.
If the person at the front did not eat, they are skipped but KEEP their place at the front. They wash at the next meal they eat.
The stand-in who washed in their place goes to the back as normal, so nobody is asked twice while someone else's turn is still pending.
Anyone who has not yet washed this month sits ahead of everyone who has, in M1?M5 order.
Being absent never creates a debt. Someone away all month simply never washes.
If Lunch? or Dinner? is not Yes, that meal's washers show — and the queue does not move for it. The other meal is unaffected.
Same as the meal not being provided: Washer = —, queue unchanged.
If exactly one person ate that meal, that person washes it.
If only two people ate, only those two are considered. The rest are ignored for that meal and owe nothing.
Totals are never forced to match. Uneven counts are the correct outcome — fairness comes from the queue, not the totals.
